summary:
Junior Astronaut: Outpost is a browser-based 3D simulation game where kids aged 7–12 command a lunar or Martian outpost for a 20-day mission with a crew of four. Players balance life support, radiation shielding, power, food, water and communication delay. Every choice has consequences, and after each day the game explains “why it happened” in simple words.

The game is built on real NASA data, not invented numbers. Live space weather comes from NASA DONKI. Real solar storms from 2003 and 2014 drive the radiation events. Mars radiation levels are based on Curiosity RAD measurements, and crew needs come from NASA’s BVAD life-support reference. Every data source is credited inside the game.

Many kids find space science abstract and hard to relate to. Our game makes it hands-on: children learn by doing, by making mistakes and trying again. Two difficulty levels (Cadet and Engineer), a mission code for classrooms, and a full Russian/English toggle make it usable in schools around the world. It runs in any browser, including on phones, with nothing to install.
details:
What it does. Junior Astronaut: Outpost is a 3D browser game where kids aged 7–12 command a base on the Moon or Mars for 20 days with a crew of four. Each day they share limited power between life support, radiation shielding, food production, comms and science. Then the day plays out, and a “Why did this happen?” screen explains the result in simple words.

Real NASA data. Live space weather comes from the NASA DONKI API. The historical solar storms of 2003 (Halloween storms) and 2014 drive radiation events. Mars radiation dose is based on Curiosity RAD, crew consumables come from NASA BVAD, and we also use OSDR and JPL sources. Every source is credited inside the game. No data is shown as “live” when it is not.

Benefits and impact. Kids learn by doing: they experiment, fail safely and try again. Abstract topics like radiation, closed-loop life support and signal delay become decisions they feel. Cadet and Engineer levels, a classroom mission code and a full RU/EN toggle make it ready for schools. It runs in any browser, including phones, with no install.

Tools. JavaScript, HTML/CSS and three.js for the 3D world, Blender with Python scripts for the 3D models, and hosting on Vercel. The source code is on GitHub. We also made an experimental Unreal Engine 5 (C++) version.

Creativity. One game combines survival strategy, a walkable 3D base, a crew you can talk to and real space-weather events, all designed for kids.
